claims.summary: Observed: dialogue_runtime.rs implements a non-destructive marker scanner; scan_known_model_control_markers (L114) preserves the remainder while identifying markers, and exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199) distinguishes quoted/grouped/explicit relations; requested token bands (L8) are separate from felt pressure.
claims.disposition: verified_existing. Complete source at SHA 902a0358 confirms the mechanism: scan_known_model_control_markers L114-144 rebuilds a remainder and pushes a marker's bytes back only when reference_syntax.is_some() (L129-131); exact_reference_delimiter_syntax L199-229 + exact_reference_delimiter_pair L153-197 classify Quoted/Grouped/Explicit; dialogue_requested_token_band L8-16 is deliberately doc-separated from felt/spectral meaning. Description is accurate.

claims.summary: Likely Snag: first_word_after (L89) uses split_whitespace() + a manual alphanumeric filter (L92); a marker followed by a punctuation-heavy string or non-standard whitespace could be handled differently than a clean word, making reference_syntax return None and the marker be stripped or improperly preserved (L124-L132).
claims.disposition: verified_existing; concern preserved, mechanism contradicted. find(|w| !w.is_empty()) (L93) skips punctuation-only chunks to the next real word; trim_matches (L92) strips surrounding non-alphanumerics, so an allowlisted relation survives punctuation/whitespace and the marker stays; strips (fails closed) only when NO alphanumeric word follows. Grounded: committed tests L2987 (punct+fail-closed), L3029 (NBSP); improper-preservation ruled out by negatives L2568/L2682-2727/L2757.
